topic: Exact request-to-effect ancestry prerequisite for safe idempotent response replay

source_derived_current_state.v16_request_ledger: frank_ingress_request_admissions stores request_key_hash/request_id_hash plus execution/epoch/credential/session/client and admission state; no completed response receipt exists.
source_derived_current_state.token_ingress: One live execution can admit multiple distinct follow-up request IDs; durable replay currently reports response_replay_available=false.
source_derived_current_state.effect_execution_fence: effect_execution_generation_fences binds effect to execution_id, lease_epoch, credential_fingerprint, session/client hashes and capability fingerprint, but no exact request_key_hash.
source_derived_current_state.v17_terminal_guard: V17 requires existence of an ingress admission matching the effect execution generation, but does not require one exact request key and effect_reentry_bindings_v17 has no request key.
source_derived_current_state.consequence: Execution-generation identity is necessary but insufficient to identify which request owns an effect when multiple requests share one execution.

fresh_external_evidence.source: AWS Builders' Library - Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
fresh_external_evidence.use: Supports durable client request identifiers and returning a semantically equivalent response for an already-completed idempotent request rather than re-executing the side effect.
Concrete production pattern: save the first request result and return it for later retries of the same idempotency key.

Reinforces the design distinction that an idempotency key identifies retries of one request and must not be reused for a different payload; not used as normative authority because the draft expired 2026-04-18.

hypothesis: Current V17 execution-generation ancestry is ambiguous at request granularity: two different V16 request admissions inside one execution can both satisfy the current effect/V17 generation join for one effect, so safe response replay cannot infer exact request ownership from existing durable state.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Execution identity may implicitly correspond to one request in all real paths even though V16 exposes follow-up admissions, making an explicit request-effect edge redundant.

fusion.architecture_invariant: Never infer request ownership from execution-generation match when more than one request may inhabit the execution.
fusion.authority_invariant: Do not repair this by letting the effect caller supply a raw request id/key; exact request ancestry must be minted by the trusted ingress/request capability that already owns the durable V16 admission.
fusion.candidate_direction: Introduce a sealed request-scoped ingress capability derived from a newly ADMITTED V16 request, bind interactive effect reservation/attempt to that capability, and persist an immutable request_key_hash <-> effect_id edge plus execution-generation identity before provider execution. Then response receipts may consume that relation and V17 terminal truth.
fusion.noninteractive_effects: Do not globally require a human/token request edge for autonomous/internal effects; distinguish interactive request-bound effects from autonomous provenance paths.

next_frontier: Build request-scoped ingress capability and durable request-effect binding as an ordinary provenance repair candidate.

Negative controls: wrong request from same execution, replay admission without live request capability, cross-execution request key, stale request capability after lease release, caller-fabricated request labels.
Only after exact request-effect binding is target-green, add immutable response/result receipts and crash replay without duplicate provider/effect execution.
